The proposed subdistrict map (current)

Zoning applies to an entire block face, never parcel by parcel — so every face gets exactly one assignment, and the subarea collapses to as few subdistricts as the data supports: just two. Subdistrict 1 (single-family & duplex only) is drawn only where a block face is already entirely that. Subdistrict 2 (SF, duplex, small apartment, neighborhood office & personal service) is every other face — this is what legalizes the density-violation parcels as "small apartment" rather than requiring removal. Established use was cross-checked against Regrid's own address-point counts, not just the assessor class and SafeGraph business matches, which reclassified 44 parcels previously read as simple duplexes into small apartment buildings once their actual mailing-address count (5–17 separate addresses) was checked against the structural record. Requiring every parcel on a face to independently qualify shrinks the untouched commercial corridor to 7 parcels — almost none of it clears a unanimous-compliance bar at the whole-face level, which is the direct, honest consequence of ruling out parcel-by-parcel treatment.

About this map

Latest revision: established use is now cross-verified against Regrid's structural class and mailing-address-point count, not just the assessor's class code and SafeGraph business matches -- this reclassified 44 parcels from "duplex" to small apartment once buildings carrying 5-17 separate mailing addresses were checked against their structural record, and raised the confirmed R-5 density-violation count from 8 to 9. The proposed subdistrict system is now strictly block-face uniform -- every parcel on a face shares one assignment, no parcel-by-parcel exceptions -- and minimized to two new subdistricts plus a separate unchanged-corridor track. Requiring unanimous compliance across a whole face before a corridor face can stay untouched shrinks that untouched footprint to 7 of 296 corridor parcels.

Built from the City of El Paso's parcel and building-footprint layers, Regrid parcel/zoning attributes, SafeGraph business-location data, and El Paso Title 20 Appendices A–C, cross-checked against the City's own Legal Nonconforming registry (Planning/PlanningZoning MapServer). Front/rear/side setback orientation is estimated geometrically from each parcel's address street and should be field-verified, in particular on corner lots. Typology groupings are a rule-based reading of zoning district, dominant use, and nonconformity driver, intended to sort parcels into shared policy pathways rather than a precise legal determination for any one lot. See the companion workbook for full per-parcel methodology notes.
